explanation: The investigation bundle contains only question.md. Its section 'Named files that could not be copied into this bundle' (question.md:23-27) lists all three named files: agent-workspace/apps/web/tsconfig.app.json, agent-workspace/apps/web/tsconfig.json and agent-workspace/apps/web/src/app.test.tsx. Without them I cannot check whether tsconfig.app.json sets or inherits resolveJsonModule, which moduleResolution or module value applies, whether tsconfig.json references a project that includes src/app.test.tsx, or whether app.test.tsx is excluded from the typecheck. I also cannot see the exact import forms used for webPackage and apiPackage. The default value of resolveJsonModule in TypeScript 7.0.2 cannot be settled from the bundle either: question.md:21 says it needs the compiler to run, and nothing in the bundle records a tsc -b run. Separately, importing ../../api/package.json reaches outside the composite project's include: ["src"], so the TS6307 'not listed within the file list of project' check could also apply under tsc -b. That can only be checked with the tsconfig contents.

missing_context.reason: Shows whether resolveJsonModule, composite, moduleResolution, module, include and exclude are set, which decides whether the JSON imports type-check under tsc -b.
Shows which project references tsc -b builds and whether any shared base config supplies resolveJsonModule.
Shows the exact import statements and paths for the JSON files, and whether the file is actually in the typechecked project.
Confirms the typecheck and build commands and the TypeScript version that is actually installed.
The output of an actual npm run typecheck or build run is the only way to settle TS 7.0.2's default JSON module behavior without guessing.
